rulesetReview.currentText: Various federations and organisers / There is no single global rulebook.
rulesetReview.note: Searches found several independent organisers (WCO Battle of the Bars; World Street Workout & Calisthenics Federation mentioned only in third-party blogs; streetlifting federations ISF, WSF, FinalRep) and no IOC/GAISF-recognised global authority. Statement holds; confidence medium. [Search-snippet evidence only; page not opened — egress proxy blocked host.]

rulesetReview.currentText: Athletes perform routines on bars, judged on difficulty of dynamic and static elements, execution and creativity.
rulesetReview.note: General description is plausible, but no freestyle rulebook (e.g. WSWCF) could be found or opened. [Search-snippet evidence only; page not opened — egress proxy blocked host.]

rulesetReview.note: Streetlifting 'multilift'/endurance formats (max reps with added weight) are described in snippets; no primary rulebook opened. [Search-snippet evidence only; page not opened — egress proxy blocked host.]

rulesetReview.currentText: Head-to-head freestyle rounds judged by a panel.
rulesetReview.note: WCO Battle of the Bars (snippet): 1-v-1 battles by weight class, 10-point must scoring by 3 neutral judges, timed rounds (sources conflict: 3x4 min main events with 90 s rest vs 3x2 min prelims; a 2017 report mentions 3 min). Medium confidence. [Search-snippet evidence only; page not opened — egress proxy blocked host.]

rulesetReview.currentText: Typical standards include full lockout at the top, chin over the bar for pull-ups, no kipping, and controlled holds for a minimum time.
rulesetReview.note: Streetlifting summaries: pull-up from dead hang to chin clearly above bar, dip requires full lockout and federation-defined depth, strong swinging forbidden. Hold-time minimums not verified. Standards differ by federation. [Search-snippet evidence only; page not opened — egress proxy blocked host.]

newRulePoints.text: Streetlifting meets test 1-rep-max weighted lifts with 3 attempts each: some federations use 4 lifts (muscle-up, pull-up, dip, squat), others a pull-up + dip total. Depth/lockout standards differ between ISF, WSF and FinalRep. [Snippet-level]

WCO Battle of the Bars uses a 10-point must system with 3 neutral judges scoring strength, endurance, agility, creativity and technique over timed rounds; mouthguards reported mandatory in its Street Sport rules. [Snippet-level]

claims.statement: In moderately trained men, 4 weeks (3x/week) of progressively harder push-up variations increased bench-press 1RM similarly to bench-press training; muscle thickness changes were not significant in the abstract. [Abstract snippet]

Elastic-band push-ups matched to bench-press muscle activation (≈6RM) produced similar 6RM strength gains over 5 weeks in trained students. Adding resistance (bands/vest) keeps push-ups effective once reps get high. [Snippet]
A standard push-up loads the hands with about 64% of body weight and a bent-knee push-up about 49% — a measurable regression step. [Snippet of review citing GRF data]

Meta-analysis: low-load training (≤60% 1RM) taken close to failure gives hypertrophy similar to high-load, but heavier loading tends to give bigger max-strength gains — so add harder variations or weight for strength, not just more reps. [Snippet]

Practitioner data (CSCS coach) found eccentric-focused pull-up training helped athletes starting at zero reps; band-assisted vs eccentric comparisons circulate online but the primary study could not be verified. [Snippet; low]

The 2014 International Consensus (endorsed by NSCA, AAP) supports supervised, progressive resistance training for youth with qualified instruction; app youth guidance should align with it. [Snippet; specifics not read]

Wrist pain is very common in gymnasts (pooled ~53% in a meta-analysis, low-certainty evidence) and in recreational handstand practitioners; risk links to training intensity and hours, supporting gradual handstand volume and wrist preparation. [Snippet]

safetyReview.currentText: Warm up wrists before handstands and planche work.
Increase straight-arm skill volume slowly — elbows and wrists adapt over months.
Balance pushing with pulling to protect the shoulders.
Practise inversions with a safe bail-out and clear space.
